scope: Research-only hybrid partition pilot comparison; no global proof or demonstrated total size reduction.
interpretation: At 600 nodes the affine-first control closes 294 numeric leaves with 13 frontier cells, while forced narrow carving closes 291 numeric plus 2 Gram basin leaves with 15 frontier cells.
Forced carving confirms exact basin leaves can occur in a sound partial partition but introduces cuts even where affine leaves could already close. It does not establish compression.
The wide adaptive 200-node pilot reaches 1 basin plus 92 numeric leaves and retains 15 frontier cells; its frontier differs from the controls, so leaf counts do not quantify a global saving.
Independent stdlib replay recomputed every numeric certificate, exact basin inclusion, normalization and both branch children for all three pilot outputs.
The original LP-guided 3000-node attempt stopped at its final hash guard because a replay receipt changed; the stable 2500-node checkpoint and rejection record are retained.
